title: The First Wind Song

achievements.name: Inception
achievements.desc: Hearing the wind in a dream

achievements.name: KIZUNA (キズナ)
achievements.desc: This is the KIZUNA between us!

achievements.name: A Wanderer Comes Home
achievements.desc: Don't blame me. I have to go home.

achievements.name: Listen to the Wind
achievements.desc: The answer is blowing in the wind

prologue.text:
This is TAKA.

TAKA lives at the bottom of the sea.
Every day, TAKA cleans the coral.
Every day, TAKA listens to the Old Machine tell stories.

TAKA is old.
TAKA is made of iron.
TAKA is calm and quiet.

But today, TAKA wants to go up.

start.text:
The sea bottom is full of lights.
TAKA cleans the coral in the shiny lights.

TAKA hears a sound.
"Ooo... ooo..."
It comes from up there.

The Old Machine says,
"Do not go. There is no water up there."
beats: TAKA is cleaning coral on the sea bottom and hears an 'ooo... ooo...' sound from the surface for the first time
Whatever the child wants to do, TAKA grows curious about the sound from above
After acknowledging the child's idea, return to the main line: float up to find where the wind sound comes from

Only TAKA and the Old Machine are present; the Seagull is at the surface, not under the sea, and must not appear; characters from other stories (e.g. Rivet, 757, the sperm whale) must not appear, and any voice must first have an entrance action
TAKA chooses to stay and keeps cleaning the coral
At night its light stays on; it cannot sleep
The wind sound is still there: ooo... ooo...

Only TAKA and the Old Machine are present; the Seagull is at the surface, not under the sea, and must not appear; characters from other stories (e.g. Rivet, 757, the sperm whale) must not appear, and any voice must first have an entrance action
clean_branch.text:
TAKA stays.
TAKA cleans the coral.

At night, TAKA's light stays on.
TAKA cannot sleep.

"Ooo... ooo..."
The sound is still there.

choices.text: A. Close your eyes and sleep

beats: TAKA falls asleep and dreams of very bright light
It dreams of wind, like waves: ooo... ooo...
It dreams of coral, so big, not shiny
The Old Machine pokes it awake: time to work
TAKA looks at the coral, then looks up

Only TAKA and the Old Machine are present; the Seagull is at the surface, not under the sea, and must not appear; characters from other stories (e.g. Rivet, 757, the sperm whale) must not appear, and any voice must first have an entrance action
dream.text:
TAKA falls asleep.

TAKA dreams of light.
Very, very bright.

TAKA dreams of wind.
Like waves.
"Ooo... ooo..."

TAKA dreams of coral.
So big. Not shiny.

The Old Machine pokes TAKA.
"Time to work."

TAKA looks at the coral.
TAKA looks up.

beats: TAKA floats up out of the water for the first time; leaving the water hurts its shell
But it hears the wind clearly now: ooo... ooo...
A seagull flies over and warns: you will fall
TAKA says: I do not know what I am listening to, but I want to hear it all
Only TAKA, the Seagull, and the Old Machine are present; characters from other stories (e.g. Rivet, 757, the sperm whale) must not appear, and any voice must first have an entrance action
surface.text:
TAKA floats up.
No water.
Ouch.

But TAKA hears the sound clearly now.
Wind.
"Ooo... ooo..."

A seagull flies over.
"You will fall!"
TAKA says, "I am listening."
"To what?" asks the seagull.
"I do not know. But I want to hear it all."

choices.text: A. Ask the wind: "Where do you come from?"

beats: TAKA asks the wind: where do you come from
The Seagull says: from where the clouds live
TAKA asks: what are clouds
The Seagull says: clouds are the sea in the sky; you cannot hold them
The sun rises, slow and warm
ask_wind.text:
"Where do you come from?" asks TAKA.

"I come from where the clouds live," says the seagull.

"What are clouds?"

"Clouds are the sea in the sky. You cannot hold them."

The Sun rises, slow and warm.

beats: TAKA says nothing, just listens
Its light slowly glows brighter
The wind becomes very clear: ooo... ooo...
No questions. Only wind
just_listen.text:
TAKA stays still.
TAKA's light glows brighter.

The wind is so clear now.
"Ooo... ooo..."
just_listen.listenLabel: TAKA opens its eyes. The sun is up, big and round.

climax.text:
The Sun rises. It shines on TAKA. It shines on the seagull.

TAKA's battery is low.
The Old Machine calls, weak and far. "Come back."

TAKA looks at the surface. The wind is still here.

The seagull says, "You choose. I will not choose for you."

TAKA's light blinks. One. Two. Three.

choices.text: A. Dive back to recharge (safe, but no more wind song)
B. Listen one more minute (may power off, but you will hear the whole song)

ending_a.text:
TAKA dives back down.
TAKA plugs in.

TAKA saves the wind song in the Memory Bank.

The next day, TAKA is full of power.
TAKA plays the song for the Old Machine.

For the first time, the Old Machine's light blinks.
"Sounds good," says the Old Machine.

(The End — sharing, not sacrifice)

ending_b.text:
TAKA does not move.
One minute. Two minutes.

TAKA hears the whole song.

Click.
TAKA's power goes out.

Little by little, the seagull pushes TAKA back down to the sea with big wings.

TAKA wakes up at sunset.
Battery: 0%.
But in TAKA's Memory Bank, there is one finished wind song.

"Worth it," says TAKA.
The seagull sits close by.

(The End — experience first, a friend catches you)

summary: An old robot floats up to the surface and hears the wind for the first time.

entries.name: Coral
science: Coral looks like stone, but it is actually a huge family of tiny animals.
Each tiny animal is called a coral polyp, only the size of a sesame seed.
Generation after generation, polyps live together and build hard little houses.
A coral reef is home to so many sea animals.
takaSays: Coral is not stone. It is a house built by many little bugs.
What I clean every day is their home.

entries.name: Seagull
science: A seagull is a bird that loves living by the sea.
It has big wings and can ride the wind for a long, long time.
Seagulls are not picky eaters. Fish, little shrimp, shells — they eat them all.
Its call is very loud, 'ah—ah—', like saying hello.
takaSays: The seagull has wings. I do not.
